synonyms: Ruellia metziae var. marshii Tharp & F.A.Barkley
look_here_first: Start with the flower color and inflorescence. Ruellia metziae has conspicuously large white flowers in a terminal panicle of opposite cymes, and the upper inflorescence axes and calyx are densely stalked-glandular-hairy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural-flora list records Ruellia metziae. Travis — the species holotype is from Travis County and the UT Travis County Acanthaceae specimen index includes R. metziae. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated Williamson County treatment.

best_field_traits: upper inflorescence with dense stalked glandular hairs
morphology_keys.comparison_training: R. ciliatiflora usually has violet to purple flowers and less strikingly white corollas. R. metziae is easiest to recognize by the large white flowers plus glandular-hairy upper inflorescence.

comparisons.key_distinctions: R. metziae has large white flowers in a terminal branching inflorescence. R. humilis is conspicuously long-pilose and typically bears axillary flowers; R. drummondiana has nearly sessile axillary flowers.
